summary: Leonard John Sedgwick (1883–1925) was an Indologist who studied at Pembroke College, Cambridge, and the University of Cambridge, earning his B.A. around 1902–1905.

Leonard Swidler (1929–2026) worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at institutions including Marquette, Wisconsin-Madison, and Tübingen, he taught at Duquesne University (1960–1966) and served as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).
Leonard Woolley (1880–1960) was a scholar in history and archaeology who was educated at St John's School, Leatherhead, and studied at New College from circa 1899 to 1903.
Leonard Zwilling (1948–2021) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and completed his studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1976.

Leonard van der Kuijp (b. 1952) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, taught at the University of Washington (c. 1990–1995), and became chair at Harvard University in 1995.

Leonhard Masing (1845–1936) was a linguist who studied at the universities of Tartu, Göttingen, and Leipzig under Leo Meyer and August Leskien. He served as a docent (1880–1910) and teacher (1918–1925) at the University of Tartu.

Leonid Kulikov is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his candidate degree from the Institute of Oriental Studies. He held positions at Leiden, Ghent, and Adam Mickiewicz universities, and became a professor at KU Leuven in 2022.

Leonidas Clint (1812–1897) was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (M.A. c. 1836–1843). He later served as principal of La Martinière College (1845–1854) and Krishnagar Government College until 1857.

Leopold Pospisil (1923–2021) studied at Charles University, Willamette, Oregon, and Yale. He served as a professor at Yale University from 1956 and curator of anthropology at the Peabody Museum of Natural History from circa 1956 to 1993.

Leopold von Ranke (1795–1886) was a historian who studied at Schulpforta and the University of Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. He held a long-standing academic post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1871.

Leopold von Schroeder (1851–1920) was an Indologist who studied at Tartu, Tübingen, and Jena under Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Kuhn. He held posts at the University of Tartu (1877–1894), Innsbruck (1894–1899), and Vienna (appointed 1899).

Leopoldo de Eguílaz y Yánguas (1829–1906) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned a doctorate in law at Complutense University of Madrid by 1864 and became Professor of General and Spanish Literature at the University of Granada in 1864.
Lepel Henry Griffin (1838–1908) was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Windlesham House School and Harrow School, he served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1860 to 1889.

Leslie S. Kawamura (1935–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther and served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary (~1976–2010).

Levi H. Elwell (1854–1916) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College and Yale University, later serving as an instructor in Latin at Amherst College from 1877 to 1878.

Levi McLaughlin works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Toronto, Tokyo, and Princeton (Ph.D. 2004–2009), he held fellowships at Kokugakuin, NUS, and Iowa before becoming a professor at North Carolina State University in 2012.

Lewin Bentham Bowring (1824–1910) was an Indologist and historian educated at the East India Company College and Fort William College. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1843–1870) and as Chief Commissioner of Mysore (~1862–1870).

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his M.A. and Ph.D. from SOAS University of London. He has held positions at Munich, NTNU (2018–2020), and the University of Bonn, becoming Professor of Tibetology in 2021.

Lewis Hodous (1872–1949) was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies educated at Case Western, Hartford Seminary, and Halle-Wittenberg. He headed Fukien Union Theological Seminary (1902–1917) and was a professor at Hartford Seminary from 1917 to 1945.

Lewis Lancaster (b. 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson, became a professor at UC Berkeley around 1967, and was president at University of the West in 1992.
